newsitem.title: USA: Marriott Intl expects record year.
newsitem.headline: Marriott Intl expects record year.

text.p: Marriott International Inc, which reported improved third quarter results, said it expects a record 1996 as high room occupancy rates and room growth rates help its results.

"This was a very good summer for the lodging industry and all of our brands posted excellent results due to a combination of high occupancy levels, substantial room rate growth and increased distribution," Marriott chairman and president J.W. Marriott Jr said in a statement.
Marriott said the company's three contract service businesses achieved solid increases in sales and profits for the quarter as they continue to gain market share.
"We expect 1996 to be a record year for the company, and we are working hard to ensure that next year will be even better," Marriott said.
In the prior fiscal year, the company reported net income of $247 million, or $1.87 a share, on revenues of $8.96 billion.

For the first three quarters of 1996, Marriott International posted net income of $196 million and earnings per share of $1.44, up 25 percent and 21 percent, respectively, over comparable 1995 results.

Lodging results reflected the addition of 16,600 hotel rooms over the past 12 months, expansion of Marriott's time share unit, and improved earnings from its 49 percent stake in Ritz-Carlton. Third quarter room occupancy increased one percentage point to 80 percent.
The company's lodging group now encompasses 1,144 properties totaling about 222,000 rooms and 2,800 vacation ownership villas.

Marriott said it plans to add about 120,000 hotel rooms across its lodging brands in years 1996 through 2000, and more than 50,000 of these rooms already are in service, under construction or approved for development.
Marriott said its Contract Services sales and profits gained in the seasonally slow third quarter and the unit has continued to add accounts over the past 12 months.

Marriott Senior Living Services posted significantly higher sales and profits in the 1996 third quarter, reflecting occupancy gains to 96 percent, strong move-in rates at newer facilities, and contributions from the Forum Group communities acquired in March 1996.

At quarter-end, the division operated 69 facilities with a total of 14,400 living units, and had an additional 16 communities under construction. Marriott plans to develop at least 100 new senior living communities over the next five years.
